items.title: Europe’s Airline Supergroups Brace for a Crucial Earnings Week
items.summary: Before the Iran war, all three of Europe's largest legacy players enjoyed decent profits. A costlier second half of the year will test how much of that holds.

items.title: Sustainability Doesn’t Sell Itself — Sell It as an Experience Instead
items.summary: Experience premiums are bankable; sustainability premiums are not. Both poll more than 70% on the question of whether they matter to travelers, but only one shows up in wallet share.

items.title: Mount Olympus Is Finally a UNESCO World Heritage Site. Managing a Tourism Surge Is Its Next Hurdle
items.summary: After a 12-year campaign, Mount Olympus and its wider area has been inscribed as a UNESCO World Heritage Site. Tour operators welcome the designation as a boost to tourism — and environmental protection.

items.title: Who Owns Travel: The Sovereign Wealth Map of 2026
items.summary: We mapped who owns travel's physical layer in 2026 and it came back sovereign, but the money is not as patient as it used to be, and after the Saudi-UAE rift, not as unified either.

items.title: What’s Inside Every Skift Global Forum Ticket and How to Use It
items.summary: Every Skift Global Forum ticket works across six windows, from two weeks out to on-demand afterward. Attendees who use each one walk in with meetings booked, stay present in the room, and leave with the introductions that turn into next quarter's deals.

items.title: China’s Outbound Travel Recovery Has a New Problem: Not Enough Planes
items.summary: Chinese demand for outbound travel continues to grow in 2026 despite war and diplomatic fallout. What's holding the market back now isn't hesitation, it's a shortage of flights.

items.title: Google Is Leaning on Travel to Sell Its AI Ad Story
items.summary: Retail and finance drove Google's search ad revenue this quarter. But Google chose travel — IHG for its newest ad format, Booking Holdings for cloud and AI-powered transactions — to show investors where its AI business lines are converging.

items.title: Hilton Cuts Fees to Rebuild Hotel Owners’ Margins as Costs Stay Sticky
items.summary: Hilton said it wants to help owners facing squeezed margins, such as by cutting some fees. "We're spending a huge amount of time on this," says CEO Chris Nassetta.
